steakhouse-financial.Name: Steakhouse Financial
steakhouse-financial.Tagline: Largest risk curator in DeFi lending.
steakhouse-financial.Description: Steakhouse is a risk curator: it underwrites collateral, sets loan-to-value parameters and allocates depositor stablecoins across overcollateralised lending markets, which is the economic core of a money market even though the matching engine belongs to Morpho and Euler. DefiLlama classifies it under "Risk Curators" per the DefiLlama API, but the product a depositor buys is a variable-rate overcollateralised lending position. It is the single most important non-Morpho credit actor on Robinhood Chain because it curates the vaults behind Robinhood Earn per Morpho's announcement.
steakhouse-financial.LongDescription: Steakhouse is a risk curator: it underwrites collateral, sets loan-to-value parameters and allocates depositor stablecoins across overcollateralised lending markets, which is the economic core of a money market even though the matching engine belongs to Morpho and Euler. DefiLlama classifies it under "Risk Curators" per the DefiLlama API, but the product a depositor buys is a variable-rate overcollateralised lending position. It is the single most important non-Morpho credit actor on Robinhood Chain because it curates the vaults behind Robinhood Earn per Morpho's announcement. It is the largest curator in DeFi lending, curating roughly $1.5bn across 51 Morpho vaults and about 53% of Morpho's stablecoin TVL against Gauntlet's roughly $0.7bn across 63 vaults, per Steakhouse's DeFi Markets Update of 2 July 2026. Total supplied $2.402bn as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Morpho deposits grew from $1.55bn on 1 January to $1.70bn on 1 July 2026 (Steakhouse, 14 July 2026). Bad debt: the curator reports zero bad debt across the first half of 2026, and less than $0.1 of bad debt across Q1 (Steakhouse, 15 May 2026); a third-party tracker shows $0.23 cumulative bad debt (CuratorWatch curator profile). Borrowed, utilisation, supply APY and borrow APY are not published at the curator level: `n.a.`
steakhouse-financial.Differentiator: Largest curator in DeFi lending, roughly $1.5bn across 51 Morpho vaults and about 53% of Morpho stablecoin TVL.
steakhouse-financial.AuditsNote: No audits by design: Steakhouse is a risk curator and deploys no contracts of its own. Smart-contract risk sits with the venues it allocates to (Morpho, Euler, Kamino).

Incidents.title: DNS hijack via registrar 2FA
Incidents.description: Attackers social-engineered OVH Cloud's phone-based 2FA, modified DNS records for the main site and app subdomains and attempted a five-day domain transfer, freezing front-end deposits and withdrawals.

native-credit-pool.Name: Native
native-credit-pool.Description: Native Credit Pool is a lending venue where liquidity providers supply capital and market makers borrow against it, which makes it an undercollateralised or partially collateralised institutional lending desk rather than a spot venue. DefiLlama classifies it as Lending with an explicit borrowed figure of $18,380,177 (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). It is one of only two non-excluded credit protocols with live TVL on Robinhood Chain.
native-credit-pool.LongDescription: Native Credit Pool is a lending venue where liquidity providers supply capital and market makers borrow against it, which makes it an undercollateralised or partially collateralised institutional lending desk rather than a spot venue. DefiLlama classifies it as Lending with an explicit borrowed figure of $18,380,177 (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). It is one of only two non-excluded credit protocols with live TVL on Robinhood Chain. It is a credit pool purpose-built to fund market makers' inventory rather than retail leverage, documented at docs.native.org. Total supplied $37.06m, total borrowed $18,380,177, implying roughly 50% utilisation at the protocol level, as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Robinhood Chain slice: $52,570 supplied against $36,930 borrowed. Supply APY, borrow APY and bad debt are not published on any page fetched here: `n.a.`

dolomite.Name: Dolomite
dolomite.Tagline: Money market where collateral keeps its native rights.
dolomite.Description: Dolomite is a variable-rate overcollateralised money market whose distinguishing feature is that collateral keeps its native rights (staking, vesting, governance) while pledged, so users borrow against assets that continue to earn. DefiLlama classifies it as Lending with $274,263,180 borrowed against $247.92m supplied (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026).
dolomite.LongDescription: Dolomite is a variable-rate overcollateralised money market whose distinguishing feature is that collateral keeps its native rights (staking, vesting, governance) while pledged, so users borrow against assets that continue to earn. DefiLlama classifies it as Lending with $274,263,180 borrowed against $247.92m supplied (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). It supports a far wider long tail of collateral types than a pooled money market, including assets that remain productive while collateralised. Total supplied $247.92m; total borrowed $274,263,180, of which Ethereum $262,596,162, Arbitrum $8,862,277 and Berachain $2,796,205, as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Note the borrowed figure exceeds the supplied figure in DefiLlama's accounting because supplied TVL nets out borrowed collateral. Utilisation, supply APY and borrow APY per market: `n.a.`
dolomite.Differentiator: Collateral keeps its native staking, vesting and governance rights while pledged.

euler.Name: Euler V2
euler.Description: Euler V2 is a modular lending kernel: anyone can deploy an isolated vault with its own oracle, LTV and interest-rate model, and link vaults into borrowable clusters. It is a money market in the strict sense, with $602,588,217 borrowed as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API).
euler.LongDescription: Euler V2 is a modular lending kernel: anyone can deploy an isolated vault with its own oracle, LTV and interest-rate model, and link vaults into borrowable clusters. It is a money market in the strict sense, with $602,588,217 borrowed as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Permissionless vault creation with cross-vault borrowing means Euler competes as lending infrastructure that third parties build markets on, not as a single curated market. Total supplied $325.03m; total borrowed $602,588,217, of which Ethereum $313,151,621, Plasma $110,283,049, Monad $94,690,755, Avalanche $38,330,016 and Sonic $20,821,132, as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Utilisation, supply APY, borrow APY and current bad debt: `n.a.`
euler.Differentiator: Permissionless vault creation with cross-vault borrowing, lending infrastructure rather than a single curated market.
euler.AuditsNote: Euler maintains a consolidated security page listing its audit set at euler.finance/#security, the link recorded in the DefiLlama API record. Individual firm names and report dates were not resolvable from a fetched page: `n.a.`

contango.Name: Contango V2
contango.Tagline: One-click looping across external money markets.
contango.Description: Contango builds looped positions by borrowing on an underlying money market and re-supplying, so a user gets levered exposure to a rate or yield spread without managing the loop. The $44,266,567 of borrowed notional against roughly $5.49m of net supplied TVL is the signature of a looping product (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026).
contango.LongDescription: Contango builds looped positions by borrowing on an underlying money market and re-supplying, so a user gets levered exposure to a rate or yield spread without managing the loop. The $44,266,567 of borrowed notional against roughly $5.49m of net supplied TVL is the signature of a looping product (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). It aggregates looping across many external money markets rather than running its own, so it turns any third-party lending market into a one-click leverage venue. TVL roughly $5.49m; borrowed $44,266,567 as of 26 July 2026, split Ethereum $29,289,378, Arbitrum $5,252,391, Base $4,235,088, Optimism $3,245,931, Avalanche $1,131,670 (DefiLlama API). Maximum leverage: `n.a.` Yield sources: underlying money-market rate spreads on the markets it routes into. Liquidation mechanism: inherited from the underlying money market, evidenced by Contango's handling of frozen Aave rsETH markets below.
contango.Differentiator: It aggregates looping across many external money markets rather than running its own, so it turns any third-party lending market into a one-click leverage venue.
contango.AuditsNote: Audit reports are published in the repository at github.com/contango-xyz/core-v2/tree/main/audit, and the repo states there is no active bug bounty while audits are in place, with disclosures to security@contango.xyz (GitHub repo). Firm names and dates: `n.a.`

yield-basis.Name: Yield Basis
yield-basis.Tagline: Levered Curve LP exposure built to cancel impermanent loss.
yield-basis.Description: Yield Basis takes a Curve BTC/crvUSD liquidity position and levers it roughly 2x with borrowed crvUSD so that the levered LP's value tracks the underlying asset rather than the square root of price, which is levered exposure to an LP yield source. The mechanism is set out in the Yield Basis how-it-works documentation and analysed independently in Statemind's teardown of how YieldBasis really works. DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming (DefiLlama API).
yield-basis.LongDescription: Yield Basis takes a Curve BTC/crvUSD liquidity position and levers it roughly 2x with borrowed crvUSD so that the levered LP's value tracks the underlying asset rather than the square root of price, which is levered exposure to an LP yield source. The mechanism is set out in the Yield Basis how-it-works documentation and analysed independently in Statemind's teardown of how YieldBasis really works. DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming (DefiLlama API). It is the only candidate here whose leverage exists specifically to cancel impermanent loss rather than to multiply yield. TVL $132,235,841 on Ethereum as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API), the largest of the five Leveraged Yield candidates. Maximum leverage: approximately 2x, per the Yield Basis docs. Yield source: Curve BTC/crvUSD pool trading fees. Liquidation mechanism: `n.a.` from any page fetched here.
yield-basis.Differentiator: It is the only candidate here whose leverage exists specifically to cancel impermanent loss rather than to multiply yield.

origami-finance.Name: Origami Finance
origami-finance.Tagline: Folded yield-token vaults held as a single receipt token.
origami-finance.Description: Origami automates folded, or looped, positions in yield-bearing tokens: the vault repeatedly deposits a yield-bearing asset as collateral, borrows against it and re-buys the asset, delivering multiplied exposure to the underlying yield. Borrowed notional of $67,218,878 exceeds supplied TVL of $49.39m, the arithmetic signature of a folded position (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming.
origami-finance.LongDescription: Origami automates folded, or looped, positions in yield-bearing tokens: the vault repeatedly deposits a yield-bearing asset as collateral, borrows against it and re-buys the asset, delivering multiplied exposure to the underlying yield. Borrowed notional of $67,218,878 exceeds supplied TVL of $49.39m, the arithmetic signature of a folded position (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming. It packages the fold as a single-token vault position, so a depositor holds one receipt token instead of managing a loop. TVL $49.39m; borrowed $67,218,878 of which Ethereum $66,959,203 and Plasma $259,675, as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama API). Maximum leverage: `n.a.` Yield sources: yield-bearing tokens on Ethereum, Berachain and Plasma. Liquidation mechanism: `n.a.`
origami-finance.Differentiator: It packages the fold as a single-token vault position, so a depositor holds one receipt token instead of managing a loop.

deltaprime.Name: DeltaPrime
deltaprime.Tagline: Undercollateralised prime accounts for leveraged farming.
deltaprime.Description: DeltaPrime issues undercollateralised "prime accounts" that let a user borrow multiples of deposited capital and deploy the proceeds into farming strategies, which is textbook leverage farming. DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026).
deltaprime.LongDescription: DeltaPrime issues undercollateralised "prime accounts" that let a user borrow multiples of deposited capital and deploy the proceeds into farming strategies, which is textbook leverage farming. DefiLlama classifies it as Leveraged Farming (DefiLlama API, 26 Jul 2026). The borrowed capital never leaves the protocol's whitelisted strategy set, which is what allows the account to be undercollateralised. TVL $3.56m as of 26 July 2026: Avalanche $1,954,844, Arbitrum $1,608,643 (DefiLlama API). This is roughly 99% below its pre-incident scale. Maximum leverage: `n.a.` Yield sources: whitelisted Arbitrum and Avalanche farms. Liquidation mechanism: `n.a.`
deltaprime.Differentiator: The borrowed capital never leaves the protocol's whitelisted strategy set, which is what allows the account to be undercollateralised.
deltaprime.AuditsNote: PeckShield audits of v1.0, v2.0 and v2.1 among others, published at github.com/DeltaPrimeLabs/deltaprime-primeloans/tree/main/audits per the DefiLlama API record. Note that these audits predate the 2024 key-compromise incidents, which were operational rather than contract-logic failures.

Incidents.title: First key-compromise exploit
Incidents.description: An attacker gained control of an admin private key and drained roughly $6m from DeltaPrime pools, the first of two operational breaches in under two months.
Incidents.outcome: Team continued operating; a second breach followed in November 2024.

Incidents.title: Second key-compromise exploit
Incidents.description: Compromised admin keys were used to drain roughly $4.75m to $4.8m across Arbitrum and Avalanche deployments.
Incidents.outcome: Post-mortem and reimbursement plan published December 2024. Audits predate the incidents, which were operational rather than contract-logic failures.

pendle.name: Inverse Finance
pendle.similarities: Both tokenise interest to fix a rate: DBR prepays borrowing cost, YT trades the yield leg.
pendle.differences: DOLA CDP stack plus FiRM fixed-rate borrowing, distinct from Aave-style variable-rate money markets.

spectra.name: TermMax
spectra.positioning: Fixed-rate, fixed-maturity credit with built-in leverage tokens.
spectra.similarities: same yield-tokenisation category, competing on curator distribution.
spectra.differences: It combines a fixed-rate order market with a built-in leverage token in the same instrument set, which most fixed-rate venues keep separate.

spectra.name: Fira
spectra.positioning: Bond and coupon tokens splitting loans into principal and yield legs.
spectra.similarities: Both are yield-tokenisation venues on Ethereum.
spectra.differences: It runs parallel fixed-rate and variable-rate vaults over the same collateral base, letting a depositor choose the rate regime rather than the market.

sense.name: Boros
sense.positioning: Pendle's venue for trading funding rates, fixed versus floating.
sense.differences: It applies the fixed-versus-floating swap to perpetual funding rates, a yield source no other candidate in this tag addresses.

liquity.name: Curve (crvUSD)
liquity.similarities: Both are decentralized CDP borrowing venues on Ethereum with continuous or soft liquidation designs.
liquity.differences: LLAMMA soft-liquidation continuously converts collateral to crvUSD as price drops, eliminating hard liquidation cascades.

liquity.name: Sky
liquity.positioning: Stablecoins aren't built to sit still.
liquity.similarities: Both issue a decentralized stablecoin against overcollateralised positions.
liquity.differences: Protocol-set Sky Savings Rate, instant no-lockup yield via sUSDS, and the Sky Agent Network for allocator-driven deployment.

liquity.name: Inverse Finance
liquity.similarities: Both offer rate-certain borrowing against ETH-class collateral, user-set at Liquity and fixed at FiRM.
liquity.differences: DOLA CDP stack plus FiRM fixed-rate borrowing, distinct from Aave-style variable-rate money markets.

inverse-finance.name: Liquity
inverse-finance.similarities: Both offer rate-certain borrowing against ETH-class collateral, user-set at Liquity and fixed at FiRM.
inverse-finance.differences: Fully immutable, governance-minimized CDP, LUSD V1 has zero ongoing interest; BOLD V2 adds user-set rates and wstETH/rETH collateral.

inverse-finance.name: Notional Finance
inverse-finance.similarities: Both offer fixed-rate on-chain lending instruments.
inverse-finance.differences: True fixed-rate/fixed-term loans through fCash, rather than variable money-market rates, giving predictable cost of capital for borrowers and lenders.

inverse-finance.name: Pendle Finance
inverse-finance.positioning: Tokenized yield: split principal and yield (PT/YT).
inverse-finance.similarities: Both tokenise interest to fix a rate: DBR prepays borrowing cost, YT trades the yield leg.
inverse-finance.differences: The dominant yield-tokenization market: PT buyers lock a fixed rate, YT buyers go long yield, a true fixed-income primitive for DeFi, with the deepest liquidity and asset coverage in the category.
